item.title: Overseas Handler Linked To Iran Behind Foiled RAF Air Base Attack
item.description: Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police believe to be Iran.

item.title: Israelis Stream to the Ballot Box to Vote on Netanyahu’s Future
item.description: A historically high turnout and a bitterly divided electorate mean it could be weeks or longer before a new prime minister is picked.

item.title: Brazil Cancels Bolsonaro’s Passports as Questions Swirl About His Location
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, under Supreme Court investigation for alleged financial crimes, was barred from leaving Brazil after his election loss on Sunday.

item.title: Global Soccer Star Kylian Mbappé Just Apologized to China—for a Mao Zedong Meme
item.description: The striker was dropped by Chinese sponsors after laughing at an image of his face on the former Chinese leader’s body and referring to him as a “dictator.”

item.title: Oil Futures Fall as Market Holds Out Hope for Middle East Diplomacy
item.description: Oil prices fell, with U.S. benchmark crude slipping back under $100 a barrel as traders held out hopes for regional diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions.

item.title: Tech Stocks Add to Gains After Yesterday’s Anthropic Rally
item.description: The Anthropic-inspired rally yesterday is extending into day two: Tech stocks are up, pushing the Nasdaq more than 1% higher.

item.title: China Claims Strong Economic Growth, but Skeptics Question Official Figures
item.description: Beijing has reported robust growth this year, but a growing chorus of economists are asking if the numbers are accurate.

item.title: We Went to Cuba to See How the Fuel Crisis Is Forcing Havana to Open Its Economy
item.description: Watch to learn why escalating sanctions and a fuel blockade haven’t toppled Cuba’s regime but are transforming its economy.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: U.K. Fiscal Discipline in Focus Ahead of Burnham Government’s First Budget
item.description: Investors will be watching for a possible increase in the bank corporation tax surcharge, higher taxes on gambling, and changes to property taxes.

item.title: Xi Wants to Play Peacemaker. Trump Has Other Ideas for a Historic Summit.
item.description: Plus, Xinjiang goes from blacklisted to global trade hub, Xi’s purges echo Stalin’s, and Kim Jong Un makes a surprise trip to China.

item.title: Ceasefire Brokered by Melania Trump Begins in Starving Ukrainian City
item.description: The pause in fighting is designed to allow humanitarian aid into the city and evacuate those who want to go.

item.title: Italy’s Eni Expects More Gas Drilling Offshore Europe as Supply Concerns Mount
item.description: The Cronos project off Cyprus in the eastern Mediterranean lays the foundation for future drilling in the region, according to chief operating officer, Guido Brusco.

item.title: China’s Industrial Profit Growth Surged in September
item.description: China’s industrial profit growth rose 14.4% from a year earlier in September, supported by strong gains in electronics and high-tech manufacturing linked to AI and digital-infrastructure spending.

item.title: Netanyahu and His Main Opponent Disagree on Many Things—but Not Israel’s Security
item.description: The electorate’s move to the right on security issues leaves candidates little room to maneuver on Gaza, Iran and a Palestinian state.

item.title: America Needs Canada’s Aluminum. Trump’s Tariff Exposed Just How Badly.
item.description: Smelters in Quebec run on cheap hydroelectric power. The Trump administration’s 50% tariff has pushed up prices for American industry.

item.title: How Brazil’s Lula Pulled Off an Upset No One Saw Coming
item.description: Three weeks ago, even his allies expected defeat. Grassroots mobilization and fears of lost benefits fueled his stunning reversal.

item.title: Brazilian Markets Crash After Lula’s Surprise Election Win Stuns Investors
item.description: Brazil’s main stock market index dropped to a two-month low after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a surprise victory.

item.title: What María Corina Machado’s Return Means for Venezuela
item.description: The opposition leader wants to revive a political movement and persuade Washington that Venezuela needs a change of government.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Weigh U.S.-Iran Diplomacy, Saudi Attacks
item.description: Oil prices fell as traders considered diplomatic efforts to ease U.S.-Iran hostilities, while further Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns about Middle East supply risks alive.
